root_cause.text: In CFS/EEVDF, the b3d99f43c72b change stopped `put_prev_task()`/`set_next_task()` from advancing `cfs_rq::zero_vruntime`, so repeated yield-triggered slice expirations could leave `zero_vruntime` stale and too far behind the runnable tasks’ positions, breaking lag tracking especially when per-cgroup ticks are delayed.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE text says “per the fingered commit, those two no longer move zero_vruntime,” that “All that moves zero_vruntime are tick and full {de,en}queue,” and that with two yield-ing tasks “the update is never more than a single slice behind” only if `avg_vruntime(cfs_rq)` is forced at the end of every slice; the patch does exactly that by adding `avg_vruntime(cfs_rq);` in `update_deadline()` and removing it from `entity_tick()`.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The CFS/EEVDF `zero_vruntime` anchor was no longer advanced on every slice boundary after commit b3d99f43c72b, because `avg_vruntime()` was removed from `entity_tick()` and only updated on tick/full enqueue-dequeue paths, leaving runnable tasks that repeatedly `yield()` able to keep `zero_vruntime` stale and eventually overflow lag tracking.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch explicitly says `avg_vruntime(cfs_rq);` was removed from `entity_tick()` and added to `update_deadline()` with the note “slice expiration,” while the commit message explains that “those two no longer move zero_vruntime” for `put_prev,set_next_task()` and that “All that moves zero_vruntime are tick and full {de,en}queue,” which is insufficient for the yield/leapfrog case.

root_cause_review.feedback: The evidence and root-cause explanation are partially consistent with the patch, but the proposed root cause is not accurate enough. The patch/commit do not say that `zero_vruntime` was “no longer advanced on every slice boundary after commit b3d99f43c72b” in the broad way claimed; they specifically describe a yield/leapfrog case where `put_prev/set_next` no longer move `zero_vruntime`, and the fix is to call `avg_vruntime(cfs_rq)` in `update_deadline()` at slice expiration. Also, “eventually overflow lag tracking” is too vague and not directly supported by the diff or CVE text. The root cause should focus on stale `zero_vruntime` during repeated yield-induced slice expirations causing it to lag too far behind, especially with cgroup tick latency, rather than claiming a generalized failure “on every slice boundary.”

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit b3d99f43c72b56cf7a104a364e7fb34b0702828b
Author: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org>
Date:   Mon Feb 9 15:28:16 2026 +0100

    sched/fair: Fix zero_vruntime tracking
    
    It turns out that zero_vruntime tracking is broken when there is but a single
    task running. Current update paths are through __{en,de}queue_entity(), and
    when there is but a single task, pick_next_task() will always return that one
    task, and put_prev_set_next_task() will end up in neither function.
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is the stale/non-advancing `cfs_rq::zero_vruntime` when only a single task is running and the tick/yield paths do not update it. This diff explicitly fixes that. The old behavior is removed: `update_zero_vruntime(cfs_rq);` is deleted from both `__enqueue_entity()` and `__dequeue_entity()` and replaced by `avg_vruntime()` that now updates `zero_vruntime` itself via `update_zero_vruntime(cfs_rq, delta);` and returns `cfs_rq->zero_vruntime`. The commit also adds a tick-side call in `entity_tick()` with the comment `/* Pulls along cfs_rq::zero_vruntime. */ avg_vruntime(cfs_rq);`, which directly addresses the stale tracking issue. Because the shown function bodies already contain the corrective logic, the vulnerable construct is absent here and the fix is present.
